items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The jazz musician was treated like Toscanini, like a symphony musician

ctx.x: What was your first reaction to Europe like? The first time you went?

It was amazing. I mean the reaction of the audience for the musicians. I didn’t believe it. The first concert we played after we got done, 84,000 flowers were put on stage. I never saw — for a jazz concert? I never saw that. But jazz musicians, especially this was 1946 I think it was or early ’47. The jazz musician was treated like Toscanini, like a symphony musician, got the same feeling you get from the audience, they gave you that feeling of greatness. They appreciate what you did. And you were treated like…
Yeah, but it’s not quite like you’re conquering heroes or—
